title: Imidacloprid contributes to bladder cancer progression: preliminary evidence based on network toxicology, machine learning and molecular docking.
summary: Machine-learning analyses of imidacloprid-related and bladder-cancer expression data identified a five-gene prognostic signature (SREBF1, PRELP, TGFBI, TNFAIP2 and TACR3), evaluated in TCGA and two GEO cohorts. In bladder-cancer cell assays, imidacloprid exposure increased measured proliferation, migration and invasion; expression assays showed changes in four of the five genes, while TACR3 did not significantly change. The cell findings do not establish that imidacloprid causes bladder cancer in people or that the risk model improves patient outcomes.
ai_technology: Ten machine-learning algorithms and combinations analyzed CTD exposure-related genes and TCGA expression data; multivariable Cox analysis formed a five-gene risk score.
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: The prognostic signature was assessed in TCGA and external GSE13507 and GSE31684 cohorts. Cell assays measured proliferation, wound closure and invasion after exposure; RT-qPCR and western blot checked gene expression. Four genes changed in the reported assays; TACR3 did not significantly change.
evidence.unknown: The cohort analyses are retrospective and the cell assays are in vitro. Neither shows that the exposure causes bladder cancer in people, nor establishes prospective clinical utility of the prognostic model.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning models selected exposure-related expression features for prognosis; the separate cell experiments directly tested imidacloprid-associated cellular behavior.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
